correctness.rationale: The exact full-state Jacobian similarity to a symmetric matrix reduces Hurwitz stability to negative definiteness. The unregulated principal block has largest eigenvalue b(k-1)-d, giving necessity; the equality case is strictly unstable by positive cross-block coupling. The equal-regulation constructive family gives hx^2-Cx+E=0, valid positive roots, an exact 2x2 group block with determinant D(2hx-C), negative transverse eigenvalues, a stable upper and unstable lower root, and a nondegenerate fold. A standalone exact-rational checker passed 964 n/parameter/size configurations. No finite search substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: Sparse ecological interventions are naturally constrained to a limited number of species. The sharp minimum n-ceil(d/b) specifies precisely how many species must acquire nonlinear self-regulation for stable coexistence in an otherwise impossible mutualistic community, an informative structural quantity not given by unrestricted higher-order rescue. The explicit fold ceiling and stable/unstable coexistence branches quantify the cost of both insufficient regulation coverage and excessive per-species feedback. It is a complete exact classification within a natural symmetric mutualism model, not an arbitrary finite computation. Limits: homogeneous complete network and local stability only.
